The scene between Simba and Rafiki in The Lion King works because Rafiki doesn’t comfort Simba by telling him the past doesn’t matter — he teaches him that the past hurts, but you can either run from it or learn from it. It’s a simple lesson, but it becomes the moment Simba finally stops hiding from who he is.

The Lion King (1994), directed by Roger Allers & Rob Minkoff, starring Matthew Broderick, James Earl Jones, Jeremy Irons. A powerful animated epic about family, destiny, and growing into responsibility, following a young lion prince whose journey from exile to courage became one of Disney’s most timeless stories.
